title.narrative: Output 5.3. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative:
In North Kordofan and White Nile States, the private sector and selected training providers delivered market relevant trainings and apprenticeship, based on a survey for skills needs in 10 localities and 40 communities conducted in September 2020. Training workshops in 10 localities were organized for 200 master craft persons in October 2020 on quality apprenticeship for youth with a view to enhancing the country ownership in delivering quality training programmes in a sustainable manner. More than 600 apprentices were thereafter trained in carpentry, welding and automotive by March 2021. Furthermore, the Supreme Council for Vocational Training and Apprenticeships (SCVTA) endorsed 3 training plans for apprentices and five vocational training curricula in May 2021, and established apprenticeship networks in March 2020 for effective training programming with various stakeholders.
In East Darfur and West Kordofan States, the assessment of 10 TVET centres validated the need for mobile training platforms and equipment and instructional packages to deliver remote learning trainings to those that are marginalized and vulnerable. The Ministry of Education also identified four physical school facilities to be revitalized to deliver practical training programmes in person. Trades-based association was brought together to upgrade informal apprenticeship programmes for metalwork, mechanics, and woodworking, which were identified as key economic activities. With the establishment of the Local Economic Development Committees, a community-level social dialogue mechanism was also established. With the support of the African Development Bank and the Government of the Netherlands, the ILO provided capacity-building support to equip key master crafts persons with tools packages. This enabled the participation of youth in training opportunities in trades, carpentry, welding, general electric, automotive, solar, tailoring and food processing.
Utilizing the ILO's sector-specific studies and labour-intensive approaches, a number of key local agricultural economic opportunities (e.g. agricultural training in the sesame and groundnut value chains) as well as construction-related economic opportunities were identified.
The ILO supported the adoption of suitable contracting modalities to engage national and state-level service providers for: 1) short-term agricultural training, 2) trades-centered skills acquisition, and 3) on-the-job training in the construction sector. Capacity-building investments approved by local partners will allow programme counterparts to leverage the mobile/deployable training platforms that have been endorsed to provider skills training outreach to under-served areas in West Kordofan and East Darfur States.
